pairs.title: Immeuble, 1 rue Le Peletier, Paris 9e
pairs.shows: Full corner facade of an elaborate commercial/insurance building: a tall domed corner tourelle topped with an iron-crested finial, sculptural dormers, and a busy, varied roofline in place of a plain 45-degree attic — a strong example of the post-1884 discontinuity.
pairs.street: 1, rue Le Peletier, Paris 9e (architect Georges Morin-Goustiaux)

pairs.title: Castel Béranger, 14 rue La Fontaine
pairs.shows: Oblique full-facade view of Guimard's Castel Béranger: mixed brick/stone bays, sculptural iron balconies, and an irregular roofline with varied dormer forms.
pairs.street: 14, rue La Fontaine, Paris 16e (architect Hector Guimard)

pairs.title: Immeuble, 31 rue de Fleurus (album Ch. Girault)
pairs.shows: Full corner facade in raking light: a tall, steep mansard/comble roof carrying multiple distinct dormer forms (round-headed, segmental, gabled), tall chimneys, a weathervane, and iron-cresting on the balcony railings — a clean discontinuity-test image.
pairs.street: 31, rue de Fleurus, Paris 6e (architect Charles Girault; this print is filed within a Commons album titled "Immeuble avenue Henri Martin" but the photo itself is captioned 31 rue de Fleurus, Paris — the album appears to bundle several of Girault's works)

pairs.title: Castel Béranger, upward facade view
pairs.shows: Steep upward-angled view showing the roofline clearly: varied dormers, tall chimneys, and iron cresting along the parapet.
pairs.street: 14, rue La Fontaine, Paris 16e (architect Hector Guimard)

pairs.title: Castel Béranger entrance gate
pairs.shows: Detail of the whiplash wrought-iron entrance gate and carved stone surround — evidence of the enriched decorative vocabulary of the period, not the roofline itself.
pairs.street: 14, rue La Fontaine, Paris 16e (architect Hector Guimard)

pairs.title: Immeuble Lavirotte, 29 avenue Rapp
pairs.shows: Full frontal facade of Lavirotte's masterpiece: sculpted dormers and iron cresting at the roofline over an exuberant ceramic and stone facade — a textbook discontinuity-test image.
pairs.street: 29, avenue Rapp, Paris 7e (architect Jules Lavirotte; won the Ville de Paris facade competition)

pairs.title: 29 avenue Rapp, alternate view
pairs.shows: Alternate full-facade daylight view of the same building, confirming the roofline dormers and cresting from a different angle/lighting.

pairs.title: 29 avenue Rapp, roofline detail
pairs.shows: Close detail of the upper comble zone: sculpted dormers, cresting figures, and ceramic ornament at the parapet — direct close-up evidence of the elaborated roofline.

pairs.title: Immeuble Les Arums, 33 rue du Champ de Mars
pairs.shows: Full oblique facade with bow windows and dense floral art nouveau ornament in stone and iron; upper roofline partially visible at frame edge.
pairs.street: 33, rue du Champ de Mars, Paris 7e (architect Octave Raquin; won the 1902 Ville de Paris facade competition)

pairs.title: Immeuble, 130 rue Réaumur
pairs.shows: Corner building with a domed corner tourelle and an elaborate mansard/comble roofline carrying multiple dormers and iron-crested balcony railings. Construction date not given in the Commons record; rue Réaumur was cut through in 1897 and most of its buildings date circa 1898-1905, so this is stylistically consistent with the family but the exact year is left blank rather than guessed.

pairs.title: 1-3 Place Saint-Michel
pairs.shows: Grand corner Haussmannian building on a major place: tall arched shopfronts, wrought-iron balconies at 2nd and top floor, heavily dressed stone bays, steep zinc mansard with dormers -- the 'grand' end of the class range where bays/balconies/cornice are elaborated well beyond a modest building while the ground-floor arcade rhythm still reads as door-scaled openings.

pairs.title: 5-7 Place Saint-Michel
pairs.shows: Second grand corner building on the same place, giving a same-scale comparison pair: full mansard, iron balconies at two levels, arcaded ground floor with awnings -- confirms the grand-end proportions are a type, not a one-off.

pairs.title: 16 rue Etienne-Marcel
pairs.shows: Near-frontal full elevation of a comfortable-tier Haussmannian building: sculpted cartouche/cherub keystone over the entry, two tiers of wrought-iron balconies with carved consoles, pilastered bays -- a clear mid-point between plain modest housing and the palatial grand end, useful for showing door scale staying constant while balcony/window enrichment increases one notch.

pairs.title: 53 rue Blanche
pairs.shows: Excellent full-elevation frontal shot showing the family's core claim directly: a modestly sized arched double door at ground level, essentially unchanged in scale from a plainer building, below four upper floors of regularly repeated bays with wrought-iron balconies, foliate keystones and a dentillated cornice -- door stays small, everything above it grows more elaborate.

pairs.title: 31 rue Du Sommerard
pairs.shows: Frontal corner elevation, comfortable tier: pedimented window surrounds on the piano nobile, a balustraded balcony course, plain but generously sized door at grade -- again shows the door holding roughly constant scale while window dressing and balcony ironwork step up in richness going up the facade and up the class range.

pairs.title: Maison, Faubourg St Antoine 122 (vue prise en 1904)
pairs.shows: Small plain shopfront house on a faubourg street: narrow bays, unadorned window surrounds, shutters, ground-floor shops crowding a small door -- the plainest, most modest end of the range. NOTE: construction date (1730) predates the 19th-century Haussmann period targeted by this corpus; kept as the clearest legible frontal example of 'modest faubourg' massing found on Commons, flag for operator review.
pairs.street: 122 rue du Faubourg-Saint-Antoine, 12e arrondissement, Paris (photographed 1904; construction inscribed on mount as 1730, built by the hopital des enfants trouves and the famille d'Aligre)

pairs.title: Rue St Merri 17-19 (Juin 1913)
pairs.shows: Frontal shot of two narrow, plain apartment buildings on a medieval-pattern street: minimal window dressing, small iron balconettes only at a couple of floors, plain shopfronts and a small round-arched carriage door at grade -- a clean modest-tier reference with door legible and undecorated.
pairs.street: 17-19 rue St Merri, 4e arrondissement, Paris (photographed June 1913 by Henri Godefroy)

pairs.title: 2 boulevard Voltaire
pairs.shows: Clean frontal full-elevation shot of a standard, unexceptional Haussmannian building on an ordinary (not grand) boulevard: regular bays, modest balcony ironwork at two floors only, plain door under a red awning at grade, simple dentil cornice -- a useful mid-range anchor between the modest faubourg examples and the ornate comfortable/grand ones.

pairs.title: Hotel particulier, angle rue Legendre / rue Leon-Cosnard, Paris XVIIe
pairs.shows: Corner treatment on a freestanding hotel particulier: chamfered/angled corner bay in brick-and-stone banding, distinct roofline break (mansard hip turning the corner) and its own fenestration rhythm independent of the two adjoining street facades.
pairs.street: 19 rue Legendre / rue Leon-Cosnard, 17e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Hotel particulier style troubadour, 30 rue de Tocqueville, Paris XVIIe
pairs.shows: Full corner elevation of a freestanding mansion: the chamfered corner reads as its own short facade with a single bay of windows, balconies, and a dedicated mansard/dormer above, distinct in rhythm from the long facades either side.
pairs.street: 30 rue de Tocqueville, angle rue Legendre / rue Leon-Cosnard, 17e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Hotel particulier, angle rue Spontini / rue de Longchamp, Paris XVIe
pairs.shows: A restrained ashlar corner block of a hotel particulier: symmetrical three-bay corner with its own balconies and roofline, clearly a distinct short facade turning the angle between two streets.
pairs.street: angle rue Spontini / rue de Longchamp, 16e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeuble, angle boulevard de Port-Royal / rue Broca, Paris Ve
pairs.shows: Classic rounded-corner apartment block (rotonde): the curved bay carries its own vertical window/balcony rhythm and a distinct domed roof cap, clearly separate from the straight bays on each street front.
pairs.street: 46 boulevard de Port-Royal, angle rue Broca, 5e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeuble post-haussmannien, 27 boulevard Jules-Sandeau, Paris XVIe
pairs.shows: Bowed/rounded corner rotonde with sculpted keystones and its own balcony rail pattern, capped by a domed corner roof that breaks from the mansard lines of the adjoining wings.
pairs.street: 27 boulevard Jules-Sandeau, angle rue Eugene Labiche, 16e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeuble Guimard, angle rue Gros / rue de la Fontaine, Paris XVIe
pairs.shows: Art Nouveau treatment of a full-height rounded corner tower (Hector Guimard): the curved prow carries continuous stacked balconies and its own turret roof, entirely independent in rhythm from the two straight facades it joins.
pairs.street: 41 rue Gros, angle rue Agar, 16e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeubles, angle rue du Renard / rue Saint-Merri, Paris IVe (c.1895-1899)
pairs.shows: Archival photograph of an older corner building with a distinct narrow chamfered facade at the street junction, shop signage at ground floor, and a roofline/dormer treatment that reads as its own short facade rather than a repeated module.
pairs.street: angle rue du Renard / 18-20 rue Saint-Merri, 4e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeuble, angle rue Monsieur-le-Prince / boulevard Saint-Michel, Paris VIe
pairs.shows: Full-height rounded Haussmannian corner rotonde with its own dormer-ringed dome roof, continuous curved balconies, and ground-floor storefront wrapping the chamfer independently of the two straight wings.
pairs.street: 56 boulevard Saint-Michel, angle rue Monsieur-le-Prince, 6e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Old Bakery - 23 rue des Francs-Bourgeois, Paris
pairs.shows: corner shopfront with full carved-and-gilded wood boiserie, painted decorative panels, and period boulangerie/patisserie signage still in place under later shop occupancy — frontal, well lit, whole facade legible
pairs.street: 21 rue de Sévigné / 23 rue des Francs-Bourgeois, 4e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Porte cochère du 26 rue de la Tombe-Issoire octobre 2021
pairs.shows: single carriage door (porte cochère), dead-frontal, full height with stone surround and arch, street furniture (wheelie bin, delivery van) beside it giving a legible scale reference for the door as the absolute-scale ruler

pairs.title: Devanture Boulangerie 159 rue Ordener
pairs.shows: full corner boulangerie shopfront, dead-frontal, dark-blue painted woodwork with gilt lettering, painted glass panels, full storefront glazing down to a panelled base — whole facade legible

pairs.title: Devanture églomisée 20050917 — Boulangerie, rue de la Roquette corner
pairs.shows: corner boulangerie, dead-frontal, green marble-clad base, gilt raised lettering signboard, awning, full storefront glazing — clean full-facade shot
pairs.street: corner of rue de la Roquette, Paris

pairs.title: Devanture de la maison Hébrard, 8 rue Royale, 8ème arrondissement, Paris (PH23412)
pairs.shows: period photograph of a luxury foundry/gallery shopfront on rue Royale with a sculpted stone lintel relief (Bourdelle) over full-height glazed shop windows and applied bronze lettering — dead-frontal, whole facade legible

pairs.title: Comptoir Général de Brosserie, 6 rue de Vaucouleurs, Paris
pairs.shows: plain painted timber shopfront with hand-painted signage and a folding steel security grille pulled across the glazing — good example of a modest, unrestored shopfront with its original ironwork shutter

pairs.title: Detail of the facade of an old bakery at Emilio-Castelar street and Charenton street in Paris
pairs.shows: corner boulangerie shopfront ("Boulangerie Viennoise"), dead-frontal, dark marbled base, painted glass corner panels, full storefront glazing and cafe-style outdoor tables — whole facade legible
pairs.street: corner of rue Emilio-Castelar and rue de Charenton, 12e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Paris 75010 Passage du Marché - 2016-01-09
pairs.shows: row of two adjoining ground-floor shopfronts on a narrow passage — one an ornate red-and-gold "Confiseur" boutique, one a plain grilled/shuttered unit — dead-frontal, good comparison of shopfront finish levels side by side

pairs.title: Portail d'entrée du Castel Béranger (Hector Guimard)
pairs.shows: Guimard whiplash wrought-iron entrance gate (copper + blue-green iron) with sculpted stone surround -- the canonical Art Nouveau ironwork reference

pairs.title: Édicule Guimard, Metro Porte Dauphine canopy
pairs.shows: Guimard's cast-iron whiplash canopy structure with amber glass panels -- the definitive Art Nouveau ironwork motif in built form
pairs.street: Place du Maréchal-de-Lattre-de-Tassigny (Porte Dauphine), 16e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Hôtel Mezzara (Hector Guimard)
pairs.shows: Frontal townhouse facade with a full-height projecting central bay carried up past the cornice into a curved gable, plus a whiplash wrought-iron balcony rail

pairs.title: 26 rue Vavin (Henri Sauvage)
pairs.shows: The canonical Sauvage rue Vavin stepped ('à gradins') facade in white ceramic tile, terraces set back above the lower floors -- clean frontal view

pairs.title: Immeuble d'angle, 1 rue Boulard
pairs.shows: Corner Art Nouveau apartment building (architect Léon Boucher) with continuous stacked curved balconies/oriels projecting from the facade up to and past the cornice
pairs.street: 1 rue Boulard (angle 11 rue Froidevaux), 14e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Façade sur rue et square d'Orléans, 80 rue Taitbout, 9ème arrondissement, Paris
pairs.shows: flat plastered street facade with pilasters, wrought-iron balcony railings, and rusticated arched carriage entrance — pre-Haussmann envelope of a grand Restauration-era private residential enclave

pairs.title: Vue de la cour, square d'Orléans, 9ème arrondissement, Paris
pairs.shows: colonnaded courtyard facade with Ionic columns and continuous wrought-iron balcony rail — grand Restauration/Louis-Philippe classical detailing

pairs.title: Immeuble, 84 rue de la Victoire, 9ème arrondissement, Paris
pairs.shows: full street row of flat plastered facades with continuous thin wrought-iron balcony railings and shuttered windows above period shopfronts

pairs.title: Immeuble, 87 rue de la Victoire, 9ème arrondissement, Paris
pairs.shows: row of flat plastered facades with shuttered windows, thin iron balcony railings, and carved frieze band above ground-floor shops

pairs.title: 13 rue de la Tour-des-Dames, Paris 9e
pairs.shows: close frontal detail of plain plastered facade with thin scrolled/lozenge wrought-iron balcony railings — direct evidence for the family's ironwork motif

pairs.title: Cité Malesherbes, Paris 9e 2-1
pairs.shows: flat plastered facade with decorative panel reliefs and thin scrolled wrought-iron balcony railings above the gated entrance to a Louis-Philippe-era artists' cité
pairs.street: Cité Malesherbes, accès 59 rue des Martyrs, Paris 9e

pairs.title: 1-3 Place Saint-Michel
pairs.shows: Corner block: 45-degree mansard comble with round dormers, bossage-rusticated ground-floor arcades, continuous balcon filant with sculpted balustrade at 2nd floor and plain ironwork balcon filant at top (5th/6th) floor, strict cornice-line unity across the block.

pairs.title: 1-7 Place Saint-Michel
pairs.shows: Two adjacent Second Empire buildings sharing identical cornice, mansard-roof, and balcon-filant lines across the parcel boundary -- clean evidence of strict block unity.

pairs.title: Avenue de l'Opéra no. 38
pairs.shows: Near-frontal full facade: sculpted balcon filant with scrollwork balustrade at 2nd floor, plainer continuous balcon filant at top floor just under the comble, dormers with round pediments, giving a clean read of the two-balcon-band rule.

pairs.title: 50 Boulevard Magenta, caryatid detail
pairs.shows: Close detail of a sculpted caryatid (by Charles Gauthier) supporting the 2nd-floor balcon filant, with the wrought-iron balustrade of the floor above visible -- clean evidence of the ornamental treatment at the balcon-filant floor.

pairs.title: 56 Boulevard Magenta, atlas figures
pairs.shows: Close detail of paired sculpted atlas figures (by Sébastien Delarue) framing a window below a continuous ironwork balcon filant -- dated facade (1866-1867), squarely inside the canonical Second Empire window.

pairs.title: Boulevard de Sébastopol corner
pairs.shows: Corner building on one of Haussmann's first pierced boulevards: mansard comble, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor and dormer-level balustrade at top floor, ground-floor shopfronts under a rusticated base.

pairs.title: Haussmannian building with corner dome
pairs.shows: Corner pavilion with a domed roof and a row of near-identical Haussmannian buildings receding down the block, each with matching balcon-filant bands -- good block-unity evidence, oblique/receding framing.
pairs.street: Paris (exact address not recorded on Commons)

pairs.title: 105 & 107 Rue de Rennes
pairs.shows: Near-frontal facade with full-height sculpted caryatids flanking the ground-floor shopfronts, a decorated balcon filant at 2nd floor immediately above them, and a plainer continuous balcon filant at the top floor below the comble.

pairs.title: Rue Halévy dormers and comble detail
pairs.shows: Close, upward-angled detail of the mansard comble: a run of pedimented dormer windows above a continuous wrought-iron balcon filant and Corinthian-capped pilasters -- clean evidence of the roof/comble geometry and top-floor balcony band.

pairs.title: 12 Rue Halévy
pairs.shows: Full, near-frontal corner facade: rusticated bossage ground floor with round-arched openings, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor, plain ironwork balcon filant at top floor just under the mansard comble -- one of the cleanest single-image reads of the whole family's defining stack.

pairs.title: 16 rue Etienne-Marcel
pairs.shows: whole facade: mascaron heads under balcony console brackets, richly molded window surrounds with alternating pediments, wrought-iron balconies -- textbook Third Republic ornament density

pairs.title: 53 rue Blanche
pairs.shows: whole facade, frontal: carved sculpted keystones/roundels above two window bands and an arched porte-cochere with carved surround -- 45-degree-comble roofline visible above

pairs.title: Immeuble haussmannien (corner facade detail)
pairs.shows: close, mildly oblique crop of a corner facade: repeated carved lintel roundels above windows, dense wrought-iron balcony rows across two floor bands

pairs.title: 105 rue de Rennes, caryatids flanking window
pairs.shows: frontal detail: full-figure sculpted caryatids flanking a piano-nobile window in place of a plain console -- an extreme, dated example of window treatment becoming sculptural rather than just corniced

pairs.title: 107 rue de Rennes, caryatids flanking window
pairs.shows: frontal detail, the neighbouring building's matching pair of sculpted caryatids at a window -- same treatment as 105 rue de Rennes, confirms it as a deliberate facade-wide scheme rather than a one-off

pairs.title: 1 bis place de l'Alma, mascaron over porte-cochere
pairs.shows: sharp frontal close-up of a smiling female mascaron set in a foliate surround above a wrought-iron porte-cochere -- clean example of mascaron-as-standard-ornament over an entrance

pairs.title: 14 boulevard Saint-Michel, window pediment with mascaron
pairs.shows: sharp frontal close-up of a broken-scroll window pediment with a mascaron head at the centre flanked by fruit swags -- textbook combination of the richening pediment and the mascaron becoming standard vocabulary

pairs.title: Mascaron detail, Paris
pairs.shows: very sharp frontal close-up of a bearded male mascaron keystone -- good clean reference for carving style even though the source building/address is not recorded

pairs.title: 47 rue du Faubourg Montmartre, mascaron keystone over door
pairs.shows: sharp frontal close-up of a bearded mascaron keystone over a carved segmental-arch door pediment with fruit swags -- another clean pediment+mascaron pairing
